    21	`divRepAffGenusScheme C`. Its `rankOneAbel` is the restriction of
    22	`abelDivAffGenusSigma`, after applying the corresponding Sigma extension. No placeholder locus,
    23	inverse, representability witness, or endgame theorem is postulated here.

    42	/-- The widened Abel transformation into the intrinsic degree-`n` Picard layer. -/

    44	  app T := ↾fun s => ⟨abelDivAff' C n T.unop s, fun K _ _ t => degAt_abelDivAff' s t⟩

    46	    ext s
    47	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    48	    exact (picEtMap_abelDivAff' g.unop s).symm

    51	lemma abelDivAffTrans_app_coe
    52	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZarAff C n T.unop) :
    53	    ((abelDivAffTrans C n).app T s).1 = abelDivAff' C n T.unop s :=
    54	  rfl

    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)

    60

    62	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/

    64	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
    65	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))

    67	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
    68	representer. -/
    69	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
    70	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    71	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
    72	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
    73	
    74	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    75	def rankOneAbelAff :
    76	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
    77	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
    78	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
    79	
    80	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    81	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
    82	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
    83	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
    84	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
    85	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
    86	
    87	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
    88	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
    89	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
    90	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
    91	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi

    12	/-!
    13	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    14	
    15	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    16	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    17	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    18	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    19	
    20	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    21	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    22	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    23	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    24	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    25	
    26	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    27	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    28	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    29	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    30	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    31	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    32	-/

--- AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean
295 AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean
     1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffZar
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The chart-typed → widened comparison (R2, human decision I-0492)
    10	
    11	The widened lane (`DivisorFamilyAff*.lean`) is worth nothing to the DD-R chain until every
    12	certificate the chart-typed design already produced instantiates it.  That is this file: the
    13	migration of a `DivisorAdaptation` (over a `FinCoverData`, i.e. basic opens of the two pinned
    14	`P¹` charts) to an `AffAdaptation` over the widened cover `FinCoverData.toAffCoverData`,
    15	CERTIFICATE INCLUDED, and the induced map `DivFamZar → DivFamZarAff`.
    16	
    17	## Why it is nearly free, and where the one real step is
    18	
    19	`toAffCoverData.pieces j` is *definitionally* `D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)`, so the
    20	section rings, the equations, the colength modules, the overlap ideals and both overlap arrows
    21	are the ORIGINAL ones read at a relabelled index — every comparison below that looks like it
    22	needs a transport is `rfl`.  Clauses (c1) therefore transport pointwise.
    23	
    24	The one real step is the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4): `gluedSubmodule` is a kernel inside
    25	`∀ j : index, colength j`, so it must be carried along the index equivalence.  The transport
    26	is `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`, used in the `symm` direction because that direction evaluates
    27	CAST-FREE (`(piCongrLeft φ e).symm g j = g (e j)`), which is what keeps the intertwining
    28	proofs from drowning in `Eq.mpr`s.
    29	
    30	## Main declarations
    31	
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.toAff` — the widened adaptation of a chart-typed one.
    33	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedCongr` — the glued modules agree, along `piCongrLeft.symm`.
    34	* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_toAff` — the certificate migrates, all seven clauses.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.toAff` — the certified family migrates.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` — the chart-typed pin
    37	  implies the widened one.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.toAff` — the induced map of functor values, compatible with
    39	  `picClass`.
    40	-/
    41	
    42	set_option autoImplicit false
    43	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    44	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    45	
    46	universe u
    47	
    48	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    49	
    50	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    51	
    52	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    53	
    54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    55	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    56	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
    57	
    58	namespace DivisorAdaptation
    59	
    60	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
    61	
    62	/-- **The widened adaptation of a chart-typed one.**  No transport: the pieces of
    63	`toAffCoverData` are definitionally the old pieces at the relabelled index, so the equation
    64	and the refinement clause carry over by `rfl`. -/
    65	noncomputable def toAff : AffAdaptation A.toFinCoverData.toAffCoverData d where
    66	  eqn := fun j => A.eqn (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)
    67	  eqn_rel := fun j y => A.eqn_rel (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) y
    68	
    69	@[simp]
    70	lemma toAff_eqn (j : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁)) : A.toAff.eqn j = A.eqn (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) := rfl
    71	
    72	/-- The relabelling equivalence: the widened index `Fin (m₀ + m₁)` against the chart-typed
    73	`Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/
    74	abbrev reindexEquiv : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁) ≃ A.index := finSumFinEquiv.symm
    75	
    76	lemma colength_toAff (j : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁)) :
    77	    A.toAff.colength j = A.colength (A.reindexEquiv j) := rfl
    78	
    79	lemma ovlColength_toAff (i j : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁)) :
    80	    A.toAff.ovlColength i j = A.ovlColength (A.reindexEquiv i) (A.reindexEquiv j) := rfl
    81	
    82	lemma toOvlLeft_toAff (i j : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁)) :
    83	    A.toAff.toOvlLeft i j = A.toOvlLeft (A.reindexEquiv i) (A.reindexEquiv j) := rfl
    84	
    85	lemma toOvlRight_toAff (i j : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁)) :
    86	    A.toAff.toOvlRight i j = A.toOvlRight (A.reindexEquiv i) (A.reindexEquiv j) := rfl
    87	
    88	/-! ### The product transports
    89	
    90	Both use `piCongrLeft` in the `symm` direction, where evaluation is cast-free. -/
    91	
    92	/-- The chart-product identification. -/
    93	noncomputable def chartProdCongr : A.chartProd ≃ₗ[R] A.toAff.chartProd :=
    94	  (LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft R A.colength A.reindexEquiv).symm
    95	
    96	@[simp]
    97	lemma chartProdCongr_apply (s : A.chartProd) (j : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁)) :
    98	    A.chartProdCongr s j = s (A.reindexEquiv j) := rfl
    99	
   100	/-- The overlap-product identification, along the diagonal action on the pair index. -/
   101	noncomputable def ovlProdCongr : A.ovlProd ≃ₗ[R] A.toAff.ovlProd :=
   102	  (LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft R (fun p : A.index × A.index => A.ovlColength p.1 p.2)
   103	    (A.reindexEquiv.prodCongr A.reindexEquiv)).symm
   104	
   105	@[simp]
   106	lemma ovlProdCongr_apply (t : A.ovlProd) (p : Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁) × Fin (A.m₀ + A.m₁)) :
   107	    A.ovlProdCongr t p = t (A.reindexEquiv p.1, A.reindexEquiv p.2) := rfl
   108	
   109	/-! ### The equalizer intertwines
   110	
   111	Reindexing acts DIAGONALLY on the pair index, so the arrow at `(i, j)` of the widened
   112	adaptation is the original arrow at `(e i, e j)` — the two squares commute componentwise. -/
   113	
   114	/-- The left arrow intertwines with the product identifications. -/
   115	lemma deltaLeft_chartProdCongr (s : A.chartProd) :
   116	    A.toAff.deltaLeft (A.chartProdCongr s) = A.ovlProdCongr (A.deltaLeft s) := by
   117	  funext p
   118	  simp only [AffAdaptation.deltaLeft, deltaLeft, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   119	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   120	    chartProdCongr_apply, ovlProdCongr_apply]
   121	  rw [toOvlLeft_toAff]
   122	  rfl
   123	
   124	/-- The right arrow intertwines with the product identifications. -/
   125	lemma deltaRight_chartProdCongr (s : A.chartProd) :
   126	    A.toAff.deltaRight (A.chartProdCongr s) = A.ovlProdCongr (A.deltaRight s) := by
   127	  funext p
   128	  simp only [AffAdaptation.deltaRight, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   129	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply,
   130	    chartProdCongr_apply, ovlProdCongr_apply]
   131	  rw [toOvlRight_toAff]
   132	  rfl
   133	
   134	/-- **Membership in the glued module transports.**  Both sides unfold to the same family of
   135	overlap identities: the widened index runs over `Fin (m₀ + m₁)`, the original over
   136	`Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`, and the relabelling is a bijection on pairs. -/
   137	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_chartProdCongr_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   138	    A.chartProdCongr s ∈ A.toAff.gluedSubmodule ↔ s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule := by
   139	  simp only [AffAdaptation.gluedSubmodule, gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker,
   140	    LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero, A.deltaLeft_chartProdCongr s,
   141	    A.deltaRight_chartProdCongr s]
   142	  exact ⟨fun h => A.ovlProdCongr.injective h, fun h => congrArg A.ovlProdCongr h⟩

   144	/-- **The glued submodule is the image of the original one.**  This is the form the three
   145	glued clauses need: `Submodule.map` of an equivalence, so `Module.Finite`, `Projective`,
   146	`rankAtStalk` and the two cokernel flatnesses all transport. -/
   147	lemma gluedSubmodule_toAff :
   148	    A.toAff.gluedSubmodule = Submodule.map (A.chartProdCongr : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] _)
   149	      A.gluedSubmodule := by
   150	  refine le_antisymm (fun t ht => ?_) ?_
   151	  · refine ⟨A.chartProdCongr.symm t, ?_, by simp⟩
   152	    exact (A.mem_gluedSubmodule_chartProdCongr_iff _).mp
   153	      (by simpa only [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using ht)
   154	  · rintro t ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
   155	    exact (A.mem_gluedSubmodule_chartProdCongr_iff s).mpr hs
   156	
   157	/-- **The glued modules are equivalent** — the map along which (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transport. -/
   158	noncomputable def gluedCongr : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.toAff.Glued :=
   159	  (A.chartProdCongr.submoduleMap A.gluedSubmodule).trans
   160	    (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ A.gluedSubmodule_toAff.symm)
   161	
   162	/-- **(c3) transports**: the inclusion cokernels are equivalent, `chartProdCongr` carrying
   163	`gluedSubmodule` onto `gluedSubmodule`. -/
   164	noncomputable def cokerInclCongr :
   165	    (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) ≃ₗ[R] (A.toAff.chartProd ⧸ A.toAff.gluedSubmodule) :=
   166	  Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _ A.chartProdCongr A.gluedSubmodule_toAff.symm
   167	
   168	/-- **(c4) transports**: the difference-arrow ranges correspond under `ovlProdCongr`. -/
   169	lemma difference_square :
   170	    (A.toAff.deltaLeft - A.toAff.deltaRight) ∘ₗ (A.chartProdCongr : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] _)

   172	  refine LinearMap.ext fun s => ?_
   173	  have hL := (A.ovlProdCongr : A.ovlProd →ₗ[R] A.toAff.ovlProd).map_sub
   174	    (A.deltaLeft s) (A.deltaRight s)
   175	  change A.toAff.deltaLeft (A.chartProdCongr s) - A.toAff.deltaRight (A.chartProdCongr s)
   176	      = (A.ovlProdCongr : A.ovlProd →ₗ[R] A.toAff.ovlProd) ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight) s)
   177	  rw [LinearMap.sub_apply, hL, A.deltaLeft_chartProdCongr, A.deltaRight_chartProdCongr]
   178	  rfl
   179	
   180	lemma range_sub_toAff :
   181	    LinearMap.range (A.toAff.deltaLeft - A.toAff.deltaRight)
   182	      = Submodule.map (A.ovlProdCongr : A.ovlProd →ₗ[R] _)
   183	          (LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) := by
   184	  have h1 : LinearMap.range ((A.toAff.deltaLeft - A.toAff.deltaRight)
   185	        ∘ₗ (A.chartProdCongr : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.toAff.chartProd))
   186	      = LinearMap.range (A.toAff.deltaLeft - A.toAff.deltaRight) :=
   187	    LinearMap.range_comp_of_range_eq_top _
   188	      (LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr A.chartProdCongr.surjective)
   189	  rw [← h1, A.difference_square, LinearMap.range_comp]
   190	
   191	/-- The difference cokernels are equivalent. -/
   192	noncomputable def cokerDiffCongr :
   193	    (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) ≃ₗ[R]
   194	      (A.toAff.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.toAff.deltaLeft - A.toAff.deltaRight)) :=
   195	  Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _ A.ovlProdCongr A.range_sub_toAff.symm
   196	
   197	/-- **The certificate migrates, all seven clauses.**  Clauses (c1) are `rfl` at the
   198	relabelled index; (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transport along `gluedCongr`, `cokerInclCongr` and
   199	`cokerDiffCongr`.  Nothing is weakened and nothing is re-proved — this is what makes
   200	"consumers port by reindexing alone" a theorem rather than a hope. -/
   201	theorem isCertified_toAff {n : ℕ} (hA : A.IsCertified n) : A.toAff.IsCertified n where
   202	  finite_colength := fun j => hA.finite_colength (A.reindexEquiv j)
   203	  projective_colength := fun j => hA.projective_colength (A.reindexEquiv j)
   204	  finite_glued :=
   205	    haveI := hA.finite_glued
   206	    Module.Finite.equiv A.gluedCongr
   207	  projective_glued :=
   208	    haveI := hA.projective_glued
   209	    Module.Projective.of_equiv A.gluedCongr
   210	  rankAtStalk_glued := fun p => by
   211	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv A.gluedCongr]
   212	    exact hA.rankAtStalk_glued p
   213	  flat_coker_incl :=
   214	    haveI := hA.flat_coker_incl
   215	    Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv A.cokerInclCongr.symm
   216	  flat_coker_diff :=
   217	    haveI := hA.flat_coker_diff
   218	    Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv A.cokerDiffCongr.symm
   219	
   220	end DivisorAdaptation

   242	/-- **The chart-typed pin implies the widened one.**  The base-side data `(m, g)` is reused
   243	verbatim; only the curve-side certificate is migrated, and the divisor equality is literally

   247	vertical fibres has no chart-typed certificate (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 4 §4.3) but

   249	theorem isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
   250	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
   251	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d := by
   252	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
   253	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
   254	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   255	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   256	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
   257	  exact ⟨G.toAff, hGdiv⟩
   258

   260	receives every chart-typed class.  Well defined because the two setoids are the same
   261	`DivEq` relation on the same underlying systems. -/
   262	noncomputable def DivFamZar.toAff {n : ℕ} (F : DivFamZar C R π n) : DivFamZarAff C R n :=
   263	  Quotient.liftOn F
   264	    (fun dp => DivFamZarAff.mk dp.1 (isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified dp.2))
   265	    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr h)

   271	      = DivFamZarAff.mk d (isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified hd) :=

   277	theorem DivFamZar.toAff_injective {n : ℕ} : Function.Injective
   278	    (fun F : DivFamZar C R π n => F.toAff) := by
   279	  intro F G h
   280	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
   281	  | h dF =>
   282	    induction G using Quotient.inductionOn with
   283	    | h dG =>
   284	      apply DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr
   285	      exact DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mp h

    12	/-!
    13	# Local generators of a finite projective module (DAT-A generators corollary)
    14	
    15	Worksheet §2.2.3a (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §4): for a finite projective module `Q`
    16	over `B` — the engine's `H⁰` on the fibrewise-vanishing locus (`datumRigidEngine`) —
    17	and a prime `p` where the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nontrivial, there is a basic open
    18	`D(f) ∋ p` and a GLOBAL element `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    19	EVERY `q' ∈ D(f)`:
    20	
    21	> Zariski-locally on `Spec B`, a fibrewise-nonzero section exists.
    22	
    23	Route: finite + projective ⟹ finitely presented + flat; `Module.freeLocus_eq_univ`
    24	gives freeness at `p`; `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers`
    25	localizes the freeness to a basic open `D(f)`; a basis element of the localized module
    26	has numerator `q`; at every `q' ∈ D(f)` the coordinate functional of the basis,
    27	composed with the away-lift `B_f →+* κ(q')` (legal since `f ∉ q'` makes `f` invertible
    28	in the residue field), evaluates the fibre image of `q` to a nonzero power of the image
    29	of `f` — no localized tensor products are formed.
    30	
    31	Consumers (stated for verbatim consumption): DAT-B's coverage (a local divisor
    32	presentation of an arbitrary functor point through DAT-A's `sectionLocalEquations`) and
    33	DD-R's local generators (dat-d-worksheet §3.4). The `Nontrivial` fibre input is the
    34	rank clause consumers hold through FLV/DAT-3.
    35	-/

    37	set_option autoImplicit false
    38	
    39	universe u
    40	
    41	open scoped TensorProduct
    42	
    43	namespace Module
    44	
    45	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] {Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module B Q]
    46	
    47	/-- If some localization of `Q` away from an element of `p.primeCompl` is trivial, the
    48	residue-field fibre at `p` is trivial: the annihilating power of `f` is invertible in
    49	`κ(p)`. -/
    50	private lemma subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away
    51	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) (f : B) (hf : f ∉ p.asIdeal)
    52	    (hsub : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)) :
    53	    Subsingleton (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    54	  have hx : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
    55	    hf (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
    56	  refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 (fun z => ?_)
    57	  induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    58	  | zero => rfl
    59	  | add u v hu hv => rw [hu, hv, add_zero]
    60	  | tmul q c =>
    61	      -- the localized image of `q` vanishes, so a power of `f` kills `q`
    62	      have hmk : (LocalizedModule.mk q 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
    63	          = LocalizedModule.mk 0 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    64	      obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := LocalizedModule.mk_eq.mp hmk
    65	      rw [one_smul, one_smul, smul_zero] at hu
    66	      -- transfer `u • q = 0` through the tensor, inverting `u` in the residue field
    67	      have hu_ne : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B) ≠ 0 := by
    68	        obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := u.2
    69	        intro h0
    70	        rw [← hn, map_pow] at h0
    71	        exact hx (pow_eq_zero_iff' .. |>.mp h0).1
    72	      have hu' : (u : B) • q = 0 := hu
    73	      have hkill : q ⊗ₜ[B] ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))
    74	          * ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c)) = 0 := by
    75	        have hz : ((u : B) • q) ⊗ₜ[B]
    76	            ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c) = 0 := by
    77	          rw [hu', TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
    78	        rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul, Algebra.smul_def] at hz
    79	        exact hz
    80	      rwa [mul_inv_cancel_left₀ hu_ne] at hkill
    81	
    82	/-- **The generators corollary** (worksheet §2.2.3a; DAT-B/DD-R's local generators):
    83	for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` with nontrivial residue-field fibre at `p`,
    84	there are `f ∉ p` and a global `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    85	**every** prime `q'` of the basic open `D(f)` — Zariski-locally, a fibrewise-nonzero
    86	section of `Q` exists. -/
    87	theorem exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective
    88	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
    89	    (hp : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    90	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Q, ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum B, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
    91	      (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
    92	  classical
    93	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
    94	  -- freeness at `p`, localized to a basic open `D(f)`
    95	  haveI hfree_p : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
    96	      (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p.asIdeal Q) := by
    97	    have hmem : p ∈ Module.freeLocus B Q := by
    98	      rw [Module.freeLocus_eq_univ]
    99	      trivial
   100	    exact Module.mem_freeLocus.mp hmem
   101	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfree, -⟩ :=
   102	    Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers p.asIdeal.primeCompl
   103	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)
   104	      (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
   105	  haveI := hfree
   106	  -- the localized module is nontrivial (else the fibre at `p` would be trivial)
   107	  haveI hnt : Nontrivial (LocalizedModule.Away f Q) := by
   108	    by_contra hns
   109	    rw [not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton] at hns
   110	    exact (not_subsingleton _)
   111	      (subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away p f hf hns)
   112	  -- a basis element, with numerator `q` and denominator a power of `f`
   113	  let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis (Localization (.powers f)) (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   114	  obtain ⟨i₀⟩ := b.index_nonempty
   115	  obtain ⟨⟨q, s⟩, hqs⟩ : ∃ ms : Q × (Submonoid.powers f),
   116	      (LocalizedModule.mk ms.1 ms.2 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = b i₀ :=
   117	    LocalizedModule.induction_on (fun m s => ⟨(m, s), rfl⟩) (b i₀)
   118	  refine ⟨f, hf, q, fun q' hq' => ?_⟩
   119	  -- the residue field of `q'` receives the away-localization
   120	  have hx : algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
   121	    hq' (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
   122	  have hxu : IsUnit (algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f) :=
   123	    isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hx
   124	  set g' : Localization (Submonoid.powers f) →+* q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   125	    IsLocalization.Away.lift f hxu with hg'
   126	  -- the evaluation functional: coordinate of the basis at `i₀`, pushed to `κ(q')`
   127	  set Λ : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₗ[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   128	    TensorProduct.lift (LinearMap.mk₂ B
   129	      (fun m c => g' ((b.coord i₀) (LocalizedModule.mk m 1)) * c)
   130	      (fun m m' c => by
   131	        rw [show (LocalizedModule.mk (m + m') 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   132	            = LocalizedModule.mk m 1 + LocalizedModule.mk m' 1 from
   133	          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (.powers f) Q).map_add m m', map_add, map_add,
   134	          add_mul])
   135	      (fun a m c => by
   136	        rw [show (LocalizedModule.mk (a • m) 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   137	            = a • LocalizedModule.mk m 1 from
   138	          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (.powers f) Q).map_smul a m,
   139	          ← algebraMap_smul (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) a, map_smul,
   140	          smul_eq_mul, map_mul, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq, ← Algebra.smul_def,
   141	          smul_mul_assoc])
   142	      (fun m c c' => by rw [mul_add])
   143	      (fun a m c => by rw [mul_smul_comm])) with hΛ
   144	  -- `Λ` evaluates the fibre image of `q` to a nonzero power of the image of `f`
   145	  intro h0
   146	  have hval := congrArg Λ h0
   147	  rw [map_zero, hΛ, TensorProduct.lift.tmul] at hval
   148	  -- compute the coordinate: `mk q 1 = s • b i₀`, and `coord i₀ (b i₀) = 1`
   149	  have hmk1 : (LocalizedModule.mk q 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = (s : B) • b i₀ := by
   150	    rw [← hqs]
   151	    change _ = (s : B) • (LocalizedModule.mk q s : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   152	    rw [LocalizedModule.smul'_mk, ← Submonoid.smul_def, LocalizedModule.mk_cancel]
   153	  have hcoord : (b.coord i₀) (LocalizedModule.mk q 1)
   154	      = algebraMap B (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) (s : B) := by
   155	    rw [hmk1, ← algebraMap_smul (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) (s : B) (b i₀),
   156	      map_smul, smul_eq_mul, Basis.coord_apply, Basis.repr_self,
   157	      Finsupp.single_eq_same, mul_one]
   158	  rw [LinearMap.mk₂_apply, hcoord, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq, mul_one] at hval
   159	  -- the value is a nonzero power of the image of `f`
   160	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := s.2
   161	  rw [← hn, map_pow] at hval
   162	  exact pow_ne_zero n hx hval

     9	/-!
    10	# The chart-typed divisor functor maps into the WIDENED one (R2)
    11	
    12	`divFamZarToAffVehicle` (`…AffVehicle.lean`) carries a chart-typed vehicle section to a widened
    13	one at each affine open of a test.  Now that both sides are functors —`divFunctor`
    14	(`DivisorFamilyZarFunctor.lean`) and `divFunctorAff` (`…AffMap.lean`) — the comparison can be
    15	stated where a consumer actually uses it: as a **natural transformation** of presheaves on the
    16	slice over `Spec k`.
    17	
    18	## Why this is the shape that matters
    19	
    20	A consumer holding a chart-typed section over a general test `T` does not want to know that the
    21	two carriers agree affine-open by affine-open; it wants to substitute the widened functor for the
    22	chart-typed one and keep its restriction maps.  That is exactly naturality, and it is the
    23	statement `DivRepGlobalData`-style clauses (which are equations between *restrictions*) can
    24	consume.
    25	
    26	The proof is one application of the widened uniqueness `divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_of`: the
    27	componentwise image of the chart-typed glued value already has the widened pullback property,
    28	because `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` turns each clause of the chart-typed `mapVal_spec` into the
    29	corresponding widened clause.  No gluing is redone.
    30	
    31	## The direction, and it is not an omission
    32	
    33	Old → new only.  A widened certificate cover is an arbitrary family of affine opens, and by
    34	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2 / ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 there is a straddling divisor at every
    35	genus `≥ 2` that no fixed pair of `P¹` charts can confine — so no natural transformation back can
    36	exist.  That failure is the content of R2 (protection I-0492), not a gap in this file.
    37	
    38	## Main declarations
    39	
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarToAffVehicle_map` — the comparison commutes with restriction along
    41	  an arbitrary morphism of test objects.
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctorToAff` — the natural transformation `divFunctor ⟶ divFunctorAff`.
    43	-/

    12	/-!
    13	# Local generators of a finite projective module (DAT-A generators corollary)
    14	
    15	Worksheet §2.2.3a (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §4): for a finite projective module `Q`
    16	over `B` — the engine's `H⁰` on the fibrewise-vanishing locus (`datumRigidEngine`) —
    17	and a prime `p` where the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nontrivial, there is a basic open
    18	`D(f) ∋ p` and a GLOBAL element `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    19	EVERY `q' ∈ D(f)`:
    20	
    21	> Zariski-locally on `Spec B`, a fibrewise-nonzero section exists.
    22	
    23	Route: finite + projective ⟹ finitely presented + flat; `Module.freeLocus_eq_univ`
    24	gives freeness at `p`; `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers`
    25	localizes the freeness to a basic open `D(f)`; a basis element of the localized module
    26	has numerator `q`; at every `q' ∈ D(f)` the coordinate functional of the basis,
    27	composed with the away-lift `B_f →+* κ(q')` (legal since `f ∉ q'` makes `f` invertible
    28	in the residue field), evaluates the fibre image of `q` to a nonzero power of the image
    29	of `f` — no localized tensor products are formed.
    30	
    31	Consumers (stated for verbatim consumption): DAT-B's coverage (a local divisor
    32	presentation of an arbitrary functor point through DAT-A's `sectionLocalEquations`) and
    33	DD-R's local generators (dat-d-worksheet §3.4). The `Nontrivial` fibre input is the
    34	rank clause consumers hold through FLV/DAT-3.
    35	-/
    36	
    37	set_option autoImplicit false
    38	
    39	universe u
    40	
    41	open scoped TensorProduct
    42	
    43	namespace Module
    44	
    45	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] {Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module B Q]
    46	
    47	/-- If some localization of `Q` away from an element of `p.primeCompl` is trivial, the
    48	residue-field fibre at `p` is trivial: the annihilating power of `f` is invertible in
    49	`κ(p)`. -/
    50	private lemma subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away
    51	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) (f : B) (hf : f ∉ p.asIdeal)
    52	    (hsub : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)) :
    53	    Subsingleton (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    54	  have hx : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
    55	    hf (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
    56	  refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 (fun z => ?_)
    57	  induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    58	  | zero => rfl
    59	  | add u v hu hv => rw [hu, hv, add_zero]
    60	  | tmul q c =>
    61	      -- the localized image of `q` vanishes, so a power of `f` kills `q`
    62	      have hmk : (LocalizedModule.mk q 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
    63	          = LocalizedModule.mk 0 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    64	      obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := LocalizedModule.mk_eq.mp hmk
    65	      rw [one_smul, one_smul, smul_zero] at hu
    66	      -- transfer `u • q = 0` through the tensor, inverting `u` in the residue field
    67	      have hu_ne : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B) ≠ 0 := by
    68	        obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := u.2
    69	        intro h0
    70	        rw [← hn, map_pow] at h0
    71	        exact hx (pow_eq_zero_iff' .. |>.mp h0).1
    72	      have hu' : (u : B) • q = 0 := hu
    73	      have hkill : q ⊗ₜ[B] ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))
    74	          * ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c)) = 0 := by
    75	        have hz : ((u : B) • q) ⊗ₜ[B]
    76	            ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c) = 0 := by
    77	          rw [hu', TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
    78	        rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul, Algebra.smul_def] at hz
    79	        exact hz
    80	      rwa [mul_inv_cancel_left₀ hu_ne] at hkill
    81	
    82	/-- **The generators corollary** (worksheet §2.2.3a; DAT-B/DD-R's local generators):
    83	for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` with nontrivial residue-field fibre at `p`,
    84	there are `f ∉ p` and a global `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    85	**every** prime `q'` of the basic open `D(f)` — Zariski-locally, a fibrewise-nonzero
    86	section of `Q` exists. -/
    87	theorem exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective
    88	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
    89	    (hp : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    90	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Q, ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum B, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
    91	      (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
    92	  classical
    93	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
    94	  -- freeness at `p`, localized to a basic open `D(f)`
    95	  haveI hfree_p : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
    96	      (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p.asIdeal Q) := by
    97	    have hmem : p ∈ Module.freeLocus B Q := by
    98	      rw [Module.freeLocus_eq_univ]
    99	      trivial
   100	    exact Module.mem_freeLocus.mp hmem
   101	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfree, -⟩ :=
   102	    Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers p.asIdeal.primeCompl
   103	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)
   104	      (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
   105	  haveI := hfree
   106	  -- the localized module is nontrivial (else the fibre at `p` would be trivial)
   107	  haveI hnt : Nontrivial (LocalizedModule.Away f Q) := by
   108	    by_contra hns
   109	    rw [not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton] at hns
   110	    exact (not_subsingleton _)
   111	      (subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away p f hf hns)
   112	  -- a basis element, with numerator `q` and denominator a power of `f`
   113	  let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis (Localization (.powers f)) (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   114	  obtain ⟨i₀⟩ := b.index_nonempty
   115	  obtain ⟨⟨q, s⟩, hqs⟩ : ∃ ms : Q × (Submonoid.powers f),
   116	      (LocalizedModule.mk ms.1 ms.2 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = b i₀ :=
   117	    LocalizedModule.induction_on (fun m s => ⟨(m, s), rfl⟩) (b i₀)
   118	  refine ⟨f, hf, q, fun q' hq' => ?_⟩
   119	  -- the residue field of `q'` receives the away-localization
   120	  have hx : algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
   121	    hq' (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
   122	  have hxu : IsUnit (algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f) :=
   123	    isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hx
   124	  set g' : Localization (Submonoid.powers f) →+* q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   125	    IsLocalization.Away.lift f hxu with hg'
   126	  -- the evaluation functional: coordinate of the basis at `i₀`, pushed to `κ(q')`
   127	  set Λ : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₗ[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   128	    TensorProduct.lift (LinearMap.mk₂ B
   129	      (fun m c => g' ((b.coord i₀) (LocalizedModule.mk m 1)) * c)
   130	      (fun m m' c => by
   131	        rw [show (LocalizedModule.mk (m + m') 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   132	            = LocalizedModule.mk m 1 + LocalizedModule.mk m' 1 from
   133	          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (.powers f) Q).map_add m m', map_add, map_add,
   134	          add_mul])
   135	      (fun a m c => by
   136	        rw [show (LocalizedModule.mk (a • m) 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   137	            = a • LocalizedModule.mk m 1 from
   138	          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (.powers f) Q).map_smul a m,
   139	          ← algebraMap_smul (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) a, map_smul,
   140	          smul_eq_mul, map_mul, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq, ← Algebra.smul_def,
   141	          smul_mul_assoc])
   142	      (fun m c c' => by rw [mul_add])
   143	      (fun a m c => by rw [mul_smul_comm])) with hΛ
   144	  -- `Λ` evaluates the fibre image of `q` to a nonzero power of the image of `f`
   145	  intro h0
   146	  have hval := congrArg Λ h0
   147	  rw [map_zero, hΛ, TensorProduct.lift.tmul] at hval
   148	  -- compute the coordinate: `mk q 1 = s • b i₀`, and `coord i₀ (b i₀) = 1`
   149	  have hmk1 : (LocalizedModule.mk q 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = (s : B) • b i₀ := by
   150	    rw [← hqs]
   151	    change _ = (s : B) • (LocalizedModule.mk q s : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   152	    rw [LocalizedModule.smul'_mk, ← Submonoid.smul_def, LocalizedModule.mk_cancel]
   153	  have hcoord : (b.coord i₀) (LocalizedModule.mk q 1)
   154	      = algebraMap B (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) (s : B) := by
   155	    rw [hmk1, ← algebraMap_smul (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) (s : B) (b i₀),
   156	      map_smul, smul_eq_mul, Basis.coord_apply, Basis.repr_self,
   157	      Finsupp.single_eq_same, mul_one]
   158	  rw [LinearMap.mk₂_apply, hcoord, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq, mul_one] at hval
   159	  -- the value is a nonzero power of the image of `f`
   160	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := s.2
   161	  rw [← hn, map_pow] at hval
   162	  exact pow_ne_zero n hx hval
   163	
   164	end Module

    10	# DAT-C C0 — the datum inverse, the divisor datum, and the canonical section
    11	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-1 + §2 (N2))
    12	
    13	Every landed datum built from a divisor family is the *twisted ideal* datum
    14	`𝒪(Θᵃ − d)` of class `θᵃ·[d]⁻¹` (G-0a). DAT-C's normalization layer needs a datum in
    15	the class `[𝒪(d)]` itself, together with its canonical section. This file pins both:
    16	
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.inv` — the **datum inverse**: same cover
    18	  data, transition units `(g i j)⁻¹`; the cocycle law inverts termwise.
    19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_inv` — the class law
    20	  `D.inv.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass⁻¹` (subordinated-cocycle level).
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relThetaCocycle_zero`, `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero`,
    22	  `thetaChartUnit_zero`, `cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero` — at exponent `a = 0`
    23	  the theta twisting cocycle is trivial, so the whole-chart theta datum has class `1`
    24	  **over an arbitrary test ring** (the worksheet cites the base-`k` class law
    25	  `cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum` + `fiberTwist_zero`; the direct `a = 0` computation
    26	  is ring-generic, which the §2 consumers need — recorded deviation).
    27	* `DivisorAdaptation.divisorDatum` — **the divisor datum**
    28	  `(A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv`, with class law
    29	  `cechPicClass_divisorDatum : A.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = d.picClass`
    30	  (G-0a at `a = 0` + the trivial theta block + `cechPicClass_inv`).
    31	* `DivisorAdaptation.canonSection` — **the canonical section is the equation system
    32	  itself** (N2): the components `(A.eqn j)` satisfy the inverse-datum matching
    33	  condition (`eqn_mul_eqnRatio` read against the inverted units), giving a global
    34	  section of the divisor datum's glued sheaf.
    35	* `DivisorAdaptation.divEq_sectionLocalEquations_canonSection` — **(N2) cut-back by
    36	  pure refinement**: the `LocalEquations` datum cut by `canonSection` (DAT-A
    37	  `sectionLocalEquations`, on any subordinated pointed cover) is `DivEq` to `d` —
    38	  the comparison units are the adaptation's own `eqn_rel` units; no fibre argument.
    39	-/

    99	              (D.unit j l))⁻¹
   100	          = ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclSnd D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
   101	              (D.unit i l))⁻¹ := by
   102	        rw [← mul_inv]
   103	        exact congrArg (·⁻¹) (D.unitsRestrict_unit_mul i j l)
   104	      have hval := congrArg Units.val key
   105	      rw [Units.val_mul] at hval
   106	      exact hval
   107	
   108	@[simp]
   109	lemma inv_pieces (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) : D.inv.pieces = D.pieces := rfl
   110	
   111	@[simp]
   112	lemma inv_unit (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (i j : D.index) :
   113	    D.inv.unit i j = (D.unit i j)⁻¹ := rfl
   114	
   115	/-- **The class law of the datum inverse**: `[D⁻¹] = [D]⁻¹`. Both classes are computed
   116	by subordinated cocycles on `D`'s canonical pointed cover by pieces, where the
   117	subordinated cocycle of the inverse datum is the inverse cocycle. -/
   118	theorem cechPicClass_inv (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
   119	    D.inv.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := by
   120	  have hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B,
   121	      D.pointedCover.opens x ≤ D.inv.pieces (D.pieceIndex x) :=
   122	    fun _ => le_rfl
   123	  have hco : gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ
   124	      = (gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   125	          (fun _ => le_rfl))⁻¹ := by
   126	    refine Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun x y => ?_
   127	    rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, inv_unitsEvInf, gluedSubordCocycle_evInf]
   128	    exact Units.ext rfl
   129	  calc D.inv.cechPicClass
   130	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
   131	          (gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   132	            hσ).class :=
   133	        (D.inv.cechPicClass_eq_mk D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ).symm
   134	    _ = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
   135	          ((gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   136	            (fun _ => le_rfl)).class)⁻¹ := by
   137	        rw [hco, OneCocycle.class_inv]
   138	    _ = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := rfl
   139	
   140	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

   142	/-! ## The theta block is trivial at exponent zero -/
   143	
   144	section ThetaZero
   145	
   146	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   147	
   148	/-- The relative theta cocycle at exponent `0` is the trivial unit: `t₀⁰ = 1`. -/
   149	theorem relThetaCocycle_zero : relThetaCocycle C B π 0 = 1 := by
   150	  change relUnitCocycle C B (fiberTwoCover π) (thetaUnit π ^ 0) = 1
   151	  rw [pow_zero]
   152	  exact map_one _
   153	
   154	/-- The theta twisting units of a finite cover datum are trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   155	theorem FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero (D : FinCoverData C B π) (i j : D.index) :
   156	    D.thetaOvlUnit 0 i j = 1 := by
   157	  rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   158	  · rfl
   159	  · rw [FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_inl_inr, relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   160	  · rw [FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_inr_inl, relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one, inv_one]
   161	  · rfl
   162	
   163	/-- The whole-chart theta transition units are trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   164	theorem thetaChartUnit_zero (i j : (thetaChartCover C B π).index) :
   165	    thetaChartUnit C B π 0 i j = 1 := by
   166	  rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   167	  · rfl
   168	  · change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _ (relThetaCocycle C B π 0) = 1
   169	    rw [relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   170	  · change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _ (relThetaCocycle C B π 0)⁻¹ = 1
   171	    rw [relThetaCocycle_zero, inv_one, map_one]
   172	  · rfl
   173	
   174	/-- **The whole-chart theta datum has trivial class at exponent `0`, over an arbitrary
   175	test ring**: all its transition units are `1`, so the subordinated cocycle is the
   176	trivial cocycle. (Ring-generic strengthening of the base-`k` route
   177	`cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum` + `fiberTwist_zero`.) -/
   178	theorem cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero :
   179	    (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).cechPicClass = 1 := by
   180	  have hco : gluedSubordCocycle (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).isGluingCocycle
   181	      (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex
   182	      (fun _ => le_rfl) = 1 := by
   183	    refine Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun x y => ?_
   184	    rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, Scheme.one_unitsEvInf]
   185	    change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _
   186	        (thetaChartUnit C B π 0 ((thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex x)
   187	          ((thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex y)) = 1
   188	    rw [thetaChartUnit_zero, map_one]
   189	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover
   190	      (gluedSubordCocycle (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).isGluingCocycle
   191	        (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex
   192	        (fun _ => le_rfl)).class = 1
   193	  rw [hco, OneCocycle.class_one, Scheme.CechPic.mk_one]
   194	
   195	end ThetaZero

   197	/-! ## The divisor datum and its class law -/
   198	
   199	namespace DivisorAdaptation
   200	
   201	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   202	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   203	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
   204	
   205	/-- The ideal transition units at exponent `0` are the plain ratio units `f_j/f_i`:
   206	the theta block is trivial. -/
   207	theorem thetaIdealUnit_zero (i j : A.index) :
   208	    A.thetaIdealUnit 0 i j = A.eqnRatio i j := by
   209	  rw [thetaIdealUnit, A.toFinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero, mul_one]
   210	
   211	/-- **The divisor datum of an adaptation** (worksheet GAP-1): the inverse of the
   212	twisted ideal datum at exponent `0` — a pinned cocycle datum in the class `[𝒪(d)]`
   213	(`cechPicClass_divisorDatum`), whose transition units are the inverted ratio units
   214	`(f_j/f_i)⁻¹`. -/
   215	noncomputable def divisorDatum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R π :=
   216	  (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv
   217	
   218	/-- **The class law of the divisor datum**: `[divisorDatum] = [𝒪(d)]` — G-0a at
   219	`a = 0`, the trivial theta block, and the class law of the datum inverse. -/
   220	theorem cechPicClass_divisorDatum : A.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = d.picClass := by
   221	  change (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv.cechPicClass = d.picClass
   222	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_inv, A.cechPicClass_thetaIdealDatum 0,
   223	    cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero, one_mul, inv_inv]
   224	
   225	/-! ### The canonical section -/
   226	
   227	/-- The value-level matching law of the equation components against the inverted ratio
   228	units: `f_i = (f_j/f_i)⁻¹ · f_j` on any open below the piece overlap. -/
   229	private lemma res_eqn_eq_inv_eqnRatio_mul (i j : A.index) {O : (relCurve C R).Opens}
   230	    (hO : O ≤ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :
   231	    (relCurve C R).resHom (hO.trans inf_le_left) (A.eqn i)
   232	      = (relCurve C R).resHom hO
   233	          (((A.eqnRatio i j)⁻¹ : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ) :
   234	            Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j))
   235	        * (relCurve C R).resHom (hO.trans inf_le_right) (A.eqn j) := by
   236	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom hO) (A.eqn_mul_eqnRatio i j)
   237	  rw [map_mul] at key
   238	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
   239	  -- key : `res f_i · res (f_j/f_i) = res f_j` on `O`; divide by the restricted unit
   240	  refine (Units.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq
   241	    ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hO (A.eqnRatio i j))).mpr ?_
   242	  rw [mul_comm]
   243	  exact key
   244	
   245	/-- The matching condition of the equation components for the divisor datum, in the
   246	exact shape of the `gluedSubmodule` carrier at `W = ⊤` (adaptation-index form; each
   247	datum-index case is definitionally this statement). -/
   248	private lemma canon_matching (i j : A.index) :
   249	    (relCurve C R).resHom
   250	        (inf_le_left : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i)
   251	        ((relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_right : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i))
   252	      = (relCurve C R).resHom
   253	          (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right :
   254	            ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)
   255	          (((A.thetaIdealUnit 0 i j)⁻¹ :
   256	              Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ) :
   257	            Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j))
   258	        * (relCurve C R).resHom
   259	            (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right :
   260	              ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces j)
   261	            ((relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_right : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j)
   262	              (A.eqn j)) := by
   263	  rw [A.thetaIdealUnit_zero i j]
   264	  have key := A.res_eqn_eq_inv_eqnRatio_mul i j
   265	    (O := ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)
   266	    (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right)
   267	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
   268	  exact key
   269	
   270	/-- **The canonical section of the divisor datum is the equation system itself**
   271	(worksheet §2 (N2)): the components `A.eqn j`, restricted to the pieces, form a
   272	matching family for the inverted ratio units — a global section of the divisor
   273	datum's glued sheaf. -/
   274	noncomputable def canonSection :
   275	    ↥(_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSubmodule R A.divisorDatum.pieces
   276	        A.divisorDatum.unit ⊤) :=
   277	  ⟨fun j => (relCurve C R).resHom
   278	      (inf_le_right.trans (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j)))
   279	      (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)),
   280	    by
   281	      intro i j
   282	      rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   283	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inl i.down) (Sum.inl j.down)
   284	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inl i.down) (Sum.inr j.down)
   285	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inr i.down) (Sum.inl j.down)
   286	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inr i.down) (Sum.inr j.down)⟩
   287	
   288	/-- The components of the canonical section are the (piece-restricted) equations. -/
   289	lemma component_canonSection (j : (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index) :
   290	    A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j
   291	      = (relCurve C R).resHom (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j))
   292	          (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) :=
   293	  Scheme.resHom_resHom _ _ _
   294	
   295	/-- The canonical section is germ-regular: its components are the adaptation's own
   296	regular equations (`eqn_regular`) — the `hreg` input of `sectionLocalEquations`,
   297	with no fibrewise hypothesis. -/
   298	theorem germ_component_canonSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   299	    (j : (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index) (y : relCurve C R)
   300	    (hy : y ∈ A.divisorDatum.pieces j) :
   301	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.divisorDatum.pieces j) y hy).hom
   302	        (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j)
   303	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk y) := by
   304	  have hy' : y ∈ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 j) :=
   305	    (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j)) hy
   306	  have hswap : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.divisorDatum.pieces j) y hy).hom
   307	      (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j)
   308	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) y hy').hom
   309	          (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) := by
   310	    rw [A.component_canonSection j]
   311	    exact TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _
   312	  rw [hswap]
   313	  exact A.eqn_regular (A.lowerIndex 0 j) y hy'
   314	
   315	/-- **(N2) — the canonical section cuts back `d` by pure refinement**: the
   316	`LocalEquations` datum cut by the canonical section on any pointed cover subordinated
   317	to the pieces is `DivEq` to `d`. The common refinement is `𝒲 ⊓ d.cover`, and the
   318	comparison units are the adaptation's own `eqn_rel` units (`relUnit`) — no fibre
   319	argument anywhere. -/
   320	theorem divEq_sectionLocalEquations_canonSection
   321	    (𝒲 : (relCurve C R).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C R → (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index)
   322	    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C R, 𝒲.opens y ≤ A.divisorDatum.pieces (σ y)) :
   323	    Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq
   324	      (A.divisorDatum.sectionLocalEquations A.canonSection 𝒲 σ hσ
   325	        (fun j y hy => A.germ_component_canonSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors j y hy))
   326	      d := by
   327	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ d.cover, fun x => inf_le_left, fun x => inf_le_right, fun x => ?_⟩
   328	  -- the piece through `x` sits inside the adaptation piece of its lowered index
   329	  have hpc : 𝒲.opens x ≤ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) :=
   330	    (hσ x).trans (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 (σ x)))
   331	  have hle : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x
   332	      ≤ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) ⊓ d.cover.opens x :=
   333	    inf_le_inf_right _ hpc
   334	  refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hle (A.relUnit (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) x), ?_⟩
   335	  -- the defining equation of the comparison unit, restricted to the refinement
   336	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom hle)
   337	    (A.res_eqn_eq_relUnit_mul (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) x)
   338	  rw [map_mul] at key
   339	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
   340	  -- collapse the constructed datum's restricted equation onto the adaptation
   341	  -- equation, term-mode (`rw` walks into the relCurve spelling seam — I-0237(a))
   342	  have hlhs := (Scheme.resHom_resHom (hσ x)
   343	      (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)
   344	      (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection (σ x))).trans
   345	    ((congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom
   346	        ((inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x).trans (hσ x)))
   347	      (A.component_canonSection (σ x))).trans
   348	      (Scheme.resHom_resHom (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 (σ x)))
   349	        ((inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x).trans (hσ x))
   350	        (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)))))
   351	  exact hlhs.trans key
   352	
   353	end DivisorAdaptation
   354	
   355	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# DAT-C C4 — the canonical-section normalization mono (N4/N5 + the local-basis companion)
    12	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §2 (N4)/(N5), GAP-3 companion)
    13	
    14	This file provides the module-theoretic heart of the canonical-section normalization —
    15	the deferred GAP-3 **Nakayama companion** (I-0253): a *given* fibrewise-nonzero element of
    16	a rank-`1` finite projective module is a **Zariski-local basis** (the converse direction
    17	of N3's generator production) — together with the DAT-A class law N4 for arbitrary
    18	fibrewise-regular sections of the divisor datum.
    19	
    20	* `Module.exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton` — **the Nakayama companion** (GAP-3
    21	  companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` of
    22	  stalk-rank `1` at `p` and an element `q` nonzero in the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)`, there is a
    23	  basic open `D(f) ∋ p` on which `x ↦ x • q` is a **bijection** `B_f → Q_f`, i.e. `q`
    24	  is a local basis of `Q`.  Route: over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is
    25	  free of rank `1`; the fibre nonzeroness pins the basis coordinate of `q` to a unit, so
    26	  `q` spans `Qₚ`; `PicardGroup`'s `bijective_of_surjective` (invertible target) upgrades
    27	  spanning to bijectivity, and `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective` spreads
    28	  the stalk bijection to a basic open.
    29	* `Module.exists_notMem_smul_eq_of_tmul_ne_zero` — **the local-rescaling corollary** (the
    30	  N5 engine input): a second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of the local basis `q`,
    31	  so `q' = a • q` in `Q_f` for a scalar `a`.
    32	
    33	Consumers: N5 (the relative uniqueness / mono engine) and the §3.2 chart mono
    34	consume the local basis to rescale the two canonical sections by a unit
    35	(the I-0231-safe route: invertibility of `H⁰`, never "fibrewise ⟹ relative").
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    40	
    41	universe u
    42	
    43	open scoped TensorProduct
    44	
    45	namespace Module
    46	
    47	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] {Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module B Q]
    48	
    49	/-- **The Nakayama companion — a fibrewise-nonzero element is a Zariski-local basis**
    50	(worksheet GAP-3 companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module
    51	`Q` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at the prime `p`, an element `q : Q` whose image in the
    52	fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nonzero generates `Q` freely on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p`: the map
    53	`x ↦ x • q` is a bijection `B_f → Q_f`.
    54	
    55	Over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is free of rank `1`, so `q`'s basis
    56	coordinate `c` satisfies: if `c` were a non-unit it would lie in the maximal ideal, hence
    57	`q` would vanish in the fibre `κ(p) ⊗ Qₚ ≅ Q ⊗ κ(p)`, contradicting `hq`. Thus `c` is a
    58	unit and `q` spans `Qₚ`; `Module.Invertible`'s `bijective_of_surjective` promotes spanning
    59	to a bijection, and the isomorphism spreads to a basic open. -/
    60	theorem exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton
    61	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
    62	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1) (q : Q)
    63	    (hq : (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
    64	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ Function.Bijective
    65	      (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f) (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)) := by
    66	  classical
    67	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
    68	  set Rₚ := Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal with hRₚ
    69	  set Qₚ := LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q with hQₚ
    70	  set mkq : Qₚ := LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q q with hmkq
    71	  -- `Qₚ` is finite, flat and hence free of rank `1` over the local ring `Rₚ`
    72	  haveI : Module.Free Rₚ Qₚ := Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
    73	  have hrank1 : Module.finrank Rₚ Qₚ = 1 := hrank
    74	  -- a basis of the free rank-`1` module, and the coordinate of `mkq`
    75	  set b : Module.Basis Unit Rₚ Qₚ := Module.basisUnique Unit hrank1 with hb
    76	  set c : Rₚ := b.repr mkq default with hc
    77	  have hmkq_eq : mkq = c • b default := by
    78	    have hsum := b.sum_repr mkq
    79	    rw [Fintype.sum_unique, ← hc] at hsum
    80	    exact hsum.symm
    81	  -- `c` is a unit: otherwise `mkq` vanishes in the fibre, contradicting `hq`
    82	  have hcunit : IsUnit c := by
    83	    rw [← IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal]
    84	    intro hcmem
    85	    -- the fibre map `κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ → κ ⊗[B] Q` sends `1 ⊗ mkq` to `1 ⊗ q`, injectively
    86	    set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField with hκ
    87	    set η : Qₚ ≃ₗ[Rₚ] Rₚ ⊗[B] Q := LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q
    88	      with hη
    89	    set ε : κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ →ₗ[Rₚ] κ ⊗[B] Q :=
    90	      (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange B Rₚ κ κ Q).toLinearMap.restrictScalars Rₚ
    91	        ∘ₗ (η.lTensor κ).toLinearMap with hε
    92	    have hηmkq : η mkq = (1 : Rₚ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
    93	      rw [hη, hmkq, LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap_apply,
    94	        LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_apply_mk, Localization.mk_one]
    95	    have hεval : ε ((1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq) = (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
    96	      simp only [hε, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
    97	        LinearEquiv.lTensor_tmul, hηmkq,

    11	
    12	Worksheet §2.2 step 2, made literal (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §3): a global section of
    13	the DAT-1 glued sheaf **is** a matching family `(s_j)` with `s_i = g_{ij}·s_j`, so once
    14	its components are germ-regular (DAT-A2, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisors`)
    15	it is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on the nose. The (1e) class law
    16	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafClass.lean`, landed while this brick was in flight) is consumed
    17	directly — the spec's `cocycleClassOn` seam is CLOSED, no interim class carrier exists:
    18	
    19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations` — the LocalEquations datum of a
    20	  germ-regular global section on **any** pointed cover subordinated to the pieces
    21	  (the (1e) subordination interface `𝒲, σ, hσ`): equations the restricted components
    22	  `D.component s (σ y)`, ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units
    23	  `gluedSubordUnit`;
    24	* `sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit` — the ratio units are **exactly** the (restricted)
    25	  transition units of the cocycle (`ratioUnit_unique`); on the piece cover the
    26	  restriction is along `≤`-reflexivity, i.e. the units themselves;
    27	* `sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle` — the units cocycle of the constructed datum is
    28	  the (1e) subordinated cocycle `gluedSubordCocycle`;
    29	* **the class law** `sectionLocalEquations_picClass`:

    31	  by a germ-regular section presents THE class of the datum's cocycle (the Abel
    32	  correspondence), through the landed `cechPicClass_eq_mk`. Naturality under
    33	  refinement/subordination-choice is the landed `gluedSubordCocycle_class_eq`; unit
    34	  rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the
    35	  landed `LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`;
    36	* `sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr` — any two germ-regular sections on any two
    37	  subordinated covers cut divisors of the same class;
    38	* `sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular` — the A2-bundled wrapper on the canonical
    39	  pointed cover (`D.pointedCover`): a fibrewise-regular global section yields the

    72	/-- The defining ratio equation of the section's restricted components on the overlaps
    73	of a subordinated pointed cover: the matching relation of the glued family, restricted
    74	from `⊤ ⊓ Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ`. -/
    75	private lemma component_ratio_eq (y y' : relCurve C B) :
    76	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
    77	        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom
    78	        ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    79	      = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
    80	            Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
    81	        * ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
    82	            𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y')).op).hom
    83	            ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y'))) := by
    84	  have hle : 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'
    85	      ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (σ y) ⊓ D.pieces (σ y') :=
    86	    le_inf (le_inf le_top (inf_le_left.trans (hσ y))) (inf_le_right.trans (hσ y'))
    87	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C B).resHom hle) (s.property (σ y) (σ y'))
    88	  rw [map_mul] at key
    89	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
    90	  change (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left
    91	      ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    92	    = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
    93	        Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
    94	      * (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_right
    95	          ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y')))
    96	  rw [gluedSubordUnit, val_unitsRestrict, component, component]
    97	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
    98	  exact key

   100	/-- **Sections ↦ divisor families** (DAT-A, worksheet §2.2 step 2): a germ-regular
   101	global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on any
   102	pointed cover subordinated to the pieces — the equations are the (restricted)
   103	components, the ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units. Germ-regularity
   104	(`hreg`) is DAT-A2's output (`germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors` relatively;
   105	`Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero` on an integral field-level curve). -/
   106	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquations
   107	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   108	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   109	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   110	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations where
   111	  cover := 𝒲
   112	  eqn y := (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y))
   113	  regular y z hz := by
   114	    rw [Scheme.resHom, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
   115	    exact hreg (σ y) z (hσ y hz)
   116	  ratio_isUnit y y' :=
   117	    ⟨gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y', D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y'⟩
   118	
   119	variable (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   120	  ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   121	    ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))

   123	@[simp]
   124	lemma sectionLocalEquations_cover :
   125	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).cover = 𝒲 :=
   126	  rfl
   127	
   128	@[simp]
   129	lemma sectionLocalEquations_eqn (y : relCurve C B) :
   130	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).eqn y
   131	      = (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)) :=
   132	  rfl

   134	/-- **The ratio units are exactly the cocycle's transition units** (worksheet §2.2 step
   135	2's "ratio units EXACTLY the cocycle"), in subordinated form: by uniqueness of ratio
   136	witnesses against a regular equation. On the piece cover the subordination is
   137	`≤`-reflexivity and `gluedSubordUnit` is the transition unit restricted along it. -/
   138	lemma sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit (y y' : relCurve C B) :
   139	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit y y'
   140	      = gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :=
   141	  ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit_unique y y'
   142	    (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y')
   143	    (D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y')).symm

   146	cocycle of the datum. -/
   147	lemma sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle :
   148	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle
   149	      = gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ :=
   150	  Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun y y' =>
   151	    ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle_evInf y y').trans
   152	      ((D.sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg y y').trans
   153	        (gluedSubordCocycle_evInf D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ y y').symm)

   156	2): the Picard class of the divisor datum cut out by a germ-regular global section of

   158	consumed on the nose through `cechPicClass_eq_mk`). -/
   159	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass :
   160	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass = D.cechPicClass := by
   161	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒲
   162	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle.class = D.cechPicClass
   163	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg]
   164	  exact D.cechPicClass_eq_mk 𝒲 σ hσ

   169	subsumed): the class of the divisor datum cut by ANY germ-regular section of the datum,

   171	rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the landed
   172	`LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`. -/
   173	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr
   174	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   175	    (s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   176	    (𝒲 𝒲' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)

   178	    (hσ' : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲'.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ' y))
   179	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),

   182	    (hreg' : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   183	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s' j)
   184	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   185	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass
   186	      = (D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg').picClass := by
   187	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg,
   188	    D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg']

   197	/-- **Fibrewise-nonzero sections cut divisors** (DAT-A + DAT-A2, bundled): over a
   198	Noetherian test ring, a fibrewise-regular global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf
   199	yields a `LocalEquations` divisor datum on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; its
   200	class is `D.cechPicClass` (`sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass`). -/
   201	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   202	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
   203	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   204	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective

   206	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
   207	  D.sectionLocalEquations s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
   208	    (fun j y hy => D.germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j (hfib j) y hy)

   213	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
   214	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   215	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   216	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   217	    (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).picClass = D.cechPicClass :=
